data.gender_notes: Anastasius is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Greek anastasis, meaning resurrection. This name was given to several early Christian saints, including Anastasius I, who ruled the Roman Empire from 491 to 518 AD and was known for his piety and justice. The name Anastasius carries the meaning “Resurrection” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Anastasius usually hope their child will grow to embody resurrection and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Anastasius total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.
data.cultural_impact: The name "Anastasius" carries a rich historical and cultural significance as it was borne by several prominent figures in early Christian Europe. Notably, Anastasius I, who was the ruler of the Eastern Roman Empire during a tumultuous time. His reign marked a period of political stability and peace, which was reflected in the name's association with resurrection and renewal. This cultural influence can still be felt today, as the name continues to be used and revered among Christians around the world.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name "Anastasius" lies in its connection to the concept of resurrection and renewal. This is reflected in the etymology of the name, which is derived from the Greek word anastasis, meaning "resurrection." For early Christians, the name "Anastasius" represented the hope and promise of a new life, and the belief that even in the face of death or hardship, there was the possibility of rebirth and renewal. This spiritual significance continues to resonate with Christians today, as the name serves as a reminder of the transformative power of faith and the promise of eternal life.
